claim.pdf_says: Table 4 — Combination of symbols in boolean expressions has a two-level header: the corner cell 'First Symbol' plus a spanning header cell 'Second symbol' printed above the five column headers 'Identifier or literal', 'B-AND B-OR B-XOR B-SHIFT-L B-SHIFT-R B-SHIFT-LC B-SHIFT-RC', 'B-NOT', '(' and ')'.
claim.markdown_says: | **First Symbol** | **Identifier or literal** | **B-AND B-OR B-XOR B-SHIFT-L B-SHIFT-R B-SHIFT-LC B-SHIFT-RC** | **B-NOT** | **(** | **)** |
claim.why_it_matters: The spanning label 'Second symbol' is the only thing that tells the reader the columns are the SECOND symbol of the pair while the rows are the first; without it the table's axes are unlabelled and a permissible-pair lookup can be read backwards. Table 3 on page 205 does keep its 'Second symbol' label, so the omission is inconsistent as well as lossy.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against the 300 dpi render of page 213 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v213/spec_p213.png) and a full-resolution crop of the header block (E:/Temp/specrecon/v213/hdr.png). Printed glyphs, read directly: Table 4's header is unambiguously TWO levels. The row-stub cell spans both header rows and reads 'First Symbol' (capital F, capital S). The upper header row spans all five data columns and reads 'Second symbol' (capital S, LOWERCASE s in 'symbol'). The lower header row carries 'Identifier or literal' | 'B-AND B-OR B-XOR B-SHIFT-L B-SHIFT-R B-SHIFT-LC B-SHIFT-RC' (printed stacked, with 'B-SHIFT-LC' broken across lines as 'B-SHIFT-' / 'LC') | 'B-NOT' | '(' | ')'. The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 9277, and the page-213.md slice line 14) collapses this to a SINGLE header row and contains no 'Second symbol' token. Ruled out the standard refutations: (a) not reflowed or on an adjacent line — a case-insensitive grep for 'second symbol' across the whole of specs/ISO_COBOL.md returns only line 8944 (Table 3), 20684 and 20734 (the two PICTURE-clause symbol tables); there is no hit anywhere in the page-213 region (lines 9270-9289); (b) not page-break furniture — Table 4's header and body sit entirely on one printed page with no break through the header; (c) not mere line wrapping or hyphenation — an entire header cell's text is absent, not re-broken; (d) neither source is misquoted — the claim's markdown quotation is byte-identical to line 9277, and the claimed PDF header text matches the render exactly. Meaning IS affected, because the matrix is asymmetric and therefore orientation-sensitive: row 'Identifier or literal' x column '(' is '—' while row '(' x column 'Identifier or literal' is 'P'; likewise row 'B-NOT' x column 'B-NOT' is '—' but row 'B-AND, B-OR, B-XOR' x column 'B-NOT' is 'P'. Transposing the axes therefore flips real conformance verdicts, and the flattened markdown invites exactly that transposition because '**First Symbol**' now occupies the position markdown treats as the header OF column 1 rather than as the two-row row-stub label it is in print. The claim's supporting comparison also checks out: the Table 3 transcription at line 8944 does retain a 'Second symbol' label ('| First symbol | Second symbol | | | |'), so the handling is internally inconsistent. Genuine content omission of printed normative table furniture; verdict real.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, with two corrections to the framing. (1) The claim overstates the damage when it says 'the table's axes are unlabelled'. Only the COLUMN-axis label is lost. The row-axis label 'First Symbol' survives in the markdown as the first header cell; a careful reader could still infer that the columns must be the second symbol. The defect is that the inference is now required where the print states it outright, and that markdown's reading of '**First Symbol**' as the header of column 1 (rather than as the corner/row-stub cell of a two-level header) actively misdirects. (2) Capitalization: the PDF prints 'Second symbol' with a lowercase 's' in 'symbol', deliberately contrasting with the corner cell's 'First Symbol'; the claim quotes it correctly in the pdf_says field but the fix should reproduce ISO's exact casing. Accurate statement of the finding: the markdown transcription of Table 4 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 9277) flattens the printed two-level header into one row and drops the spanning cell 'Second symbol' entirely; the word appears nowhere in the page-213 region. Because the permissible-pair matrix is asymmetric (row 'Identifier or literal' x col '(' = '—' vs row '(' x col 'Identifier or literal' = 'P'), the lost column-axis label is load-bearing rather than decorative. Remedy: restore a two-level header, e.g. a preceding header row reading '| First Symbol | Second symbol | | | | |' (matching how Table 3 is already transcribed at line 8944), or an explicit parenthetical note that rows are the first symbol and columns the second. Out of scope for this finding but observed while verifying: Table 3's own transcription, though it keeps the label, is separately malformed — line 8944's header carries a 5-column separator on line 8945 followed by a 6-cell row on line 8946 with an empty leading cell, and its body is split across the page-205/206 boundary at line 8957.
